title: Jude and the Kitchen
premise: Jude Calloway, a marine biologist who counts sea turtles instead of heartbreaks, agrees to pose as Silas Nystrom's girlfriend at his family's island reunion to spare them both an awkward weekend — but by dessert the fake date feels dangerously real. When Jude discovers her beloved bakery lease is expiring and Silas's family corporation is behind the eviction, love collides with duty: he must choose between loyalty to his ruthless relatives and helping Jude fight for justice outside the law. Together they rally the island community to expose the family's fraudulent land claims, risking Silas's inheritance and Jude's guarded heart. In the end, the lease is saved, Silas stays past the last train, and both learn that second chances belong to people brave enough to take them.
about_author: Mirabel Eastwick is a former pastry chef who traded early-morning ovens for late-night manuscripts, writing love stories set in coastal towns she can no longer resist visiting. She lives on a windswept peninsula with two rescue dogs and a firm belief that every romance deserves a good bread metaphor.

chapters.title: Turtle Season
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On a dawn survey, Jude logs nesting turtles while deflecting her sister's questions about her nonexistent love life. Establishes her habit of counting anything but her own loneliness. Emotional beat: wry self-protection hiding real grief over her late mother's bakery.

chapters.title: The Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A certified letter announces the bakery lease terminates in ninety days, sold to Nystrom Holdings. Jude rages, then calculates: she has one season to fight. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Man on the Ferry
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas returns to Saltmere Island for his grandmother's reunion, dreading his family's expectations. He watches Jude argue with a dockhand about turtle nets and is disarmed by her ferocity. Emotional beat: reluctant homesickness meeting unexpected curiosity.

chapters.title: Flour and Bad Ideas
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Jude storms into the marina office to confront the new landlord and finds Silas, who has no idea his family bought the building. Their argument turns into banter, then a reckless proposal. Emotional beat: sparks struck from conflict.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Over cinnamon rolls, they negotiate: she plays his girlfriend at the reunion; he stalls the lease and digs into the sale paperwork. Rules are written on a napkin. Emotional beat: cautious alliance disguised as a joke.

chapters.title: Packing the Armor
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas rehearses lies in his rental cottage and realizes he hasn't lied to his grandmother before. He packs the watch his late father left him, a reminder of what duty cost. Emotional beat: guilt arriving ahead of schedule.

chapters.title: Arrival at Nystrom House
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The reunion begins: cold marble, colder aunts, and Silas's hand warm at her back. His grandmother Vivienne sizes Jude up like a specimen. Emotional beat: performance anxiety becoming something steadier — partnership.

chapters.title: The First Real Laugh
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Trapped in a croquet match with his insufferable cousin Bram, Silas catches Jude cheating brilliantly and laughs for the first time in years. Emotional beat: the fake relationship cracking open into genuine delight.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the reunion dinner, Vivienne announces the waterfront redevelopment plan — including the bakery block. Under the table, Silas grips Jude's hand. By dessert, the fake date feels too real. Emotional beat: intimacy forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They escape the reunion and sprint for the midnight train, missing it by seconds. Stranded on the platform, they stop performing. Emotional beat: the first honest conversation, and the unspoken wish that someone would stay.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas requests the Holdings' acquisition file and finds irregularities: signatures dated when the seller was hospitalized, prices far below market. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into dread about his own name on the letterhead.

chapters.title: The Harbor Archive
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude and her friend Dot, the town archivist, dig through harbor records and find older deeds contradicting Nystrom Holdings' title claim. Emotional beat: hope with evidence attached.

chapters.title: Bram's Warning
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Bram corners Silas: stay out of the waterfront deal or lose his seat on the board — and the research funding for his turtle sanctuary. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a rope.

chapters.title: Night Survey
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude invites Silas on a night turtle survey to clear their heads. Counting hatchlings together, she tells him about her mother's bakery and the year everything fell apart. Emotional beat: vulnerability exchanged like contraband.

chapters.title: The Almost Kiss
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Back on the beach, wet and laughing, they lean close — and Silas pulls away, citing the napkin rules. Emotional beat: longing denied, which only deepens it.

chapters.title: Vivienne Summons
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Vivienne privately offers Jude money to disappear, revealing she knows the romance began as theater. Silas walks in mid-offer. Emotional beat: betrayal of trust, and Jude's dignity in refusing.

chapters.title: Broken Napkin
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts Silas: did he know about the offer? Their fight is loud, honest, and devastating. She leaves. Emotional beat: the fake relationship's collapse exposing how real it became.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles, Not Heartbreaks
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude throws herself into survey work and bakery prep, pretending the ache is just fatigue. Her sister calls her out: 'You're doing the thing again.' Emotional beat: grief recognized as love's receipt.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas confirms the deed signatures were forged — by Bram, with Vivienne's knowledge. He photographs everything, hands shaking. Emotional beat: loyalty to family dying by documented degrees.

chapters.title: Dot's Basement
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Dot uncovers a 1950s covenant: the bakery block was deeded to the town for 'community commerce in perpetuity.' A legal long shot, but a real one. Emotional beat: the fight gaining a spine.

chapters.title: An Apology in Dough
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas shows up at 5 a.m., apron on, asking Jude to teach him to bake her mother's morning buns. No excuses first — just flour, patience, and a full apology. Emotional beat: humility as courtship.

chapters.title: Revised Terms
chapters.summary: Both POVs. New napkin, new terms: no more pretending, no more secrets. This time neither of them jokes. Emotional beat: commitment without contract.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas presents the forgery evidence to the Holdings board; Bram counters by accusing Silas of leaking trade secrets. The vote suspends Silas pending investigation. Emotional beat: justice beginning to cost exactly what it should.

chapters.title: Rumors on the Dock
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Word spreads that Silas betrayed his family for the bakery girl. Some neighbors cheer; others worry the whole town will pay. Emotional beat: found family tested by public scrutiny.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Garden
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas confronts Vivienne among her roses. She admits the fraud but warns him: expose it and he loses everything she built for him. He asks what his father would have wanted. She doesn't answer. Emotional beat: generational grief surfacing.

chapters.title: The Petition
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude, Dot, and the fisherman union launch a petition invoking the old covenant, gathering three hundred signatures in two days. Emotional beat: a town discovering its own muscle.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Someone breaks into the bakery overnight — records scattered, the historic deed stolen, ovens damaged. Insurance won't cover 'pre-existing disputes.' Emotional beat: fear, then fury, then refusal.

chapters.title: Bram's Offer
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Bram offers to restore Silas's board seat if he hands over the copies of the forged deeds and drops the covenant claim. Silas asks for one night to decide. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a brother's face.

chapters.title: The Choice at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Silas walks the flats at low tide with his father's watch, then mails the evidence to the county registrar instead. Emotional beat: duty redirected toward love and truth.

chapters.title: Last Train Leaving
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Believing Silas took Bram's deal, Jude watches him board the evening ferry and doesn't call after him. Emotional beat: heartbreak mistaken for confirmation — the darkest hour.

chapters.title: What the Registrar Found
chapters.summary: Dot's POV (brief) / Jude's POV. The registrar validates the 1950s covenant and opens a fraud inquiry into the deed transfers. The town erupts in cautious celebration. Emotional beat: vindication arriving, but the win feels hollow without Silas.

chapters.title: The Hearing Notice
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas is named as a witness against his own family; Vivienne stops speaking to him entirely. Alone in the cottage, he finally reads his father's unsent letters and finds a man who once chose the island over the company. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Ovens Cold
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With the hearing days away and the bakery unusable, Jude nearly gives up. The town shows up unasked: fishermen repair the ovens, Dot brings coffee, children scrub floors. Emotional beat: found family made literal.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Before the county commission, Silas testifies to the forgeries; Jude presents the covenant and the town's petition. Bram's lawyer implodes under cross-examination. Emotional beat: quiet courage outweighing expensive counsel.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The commission upholds the community covenant and voids the fraudulent transfer; the bakery block is protected in perpetuity. Criminal referral follows for Bram. Emotional beat: justice outside the boardroom, delivered by ordinary people.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Visit
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Vivienne comes to the bakery herself, orders nothing, and leaves an envelope: the original deed, plus a single line — 'Your father would have stayed.' Emotional beat: not forgiveness yet, but the door left unlocked.

chapters.title: Lease Renewed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude signs a new twenty-year lease and reopens the bakery with a sign reading 'Calloway & Co.' — the Co. being everyone who showed up. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into legacy.

chapters.title: Past the Last Train
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Closing night, Silas misses the last train on purpose this time, standing on the empty platform until Jude comes to find him. He asks to stay — not for a weekend, but indefinitely. Emotional beat: the wish from chapter ten finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Second Chances
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue tone. One year later: turtles nesting, bakery thriving, Silas's sanctuary funded by a settlement he donated. On the napkin framed above the register, the old rules crossed out, one line added: 'Stay.' Emotional beat: love chosen daily, timing be damned.
